correctness.rationale: The baseline gauged polynomial is D_N(t)=sin((N+1)t/2)/sin(t/2), with N simple interior zeros t_j=2πj/(N+1) for even N, slopes |D_N'(t_j)|=(N+1)/(2|sin(πj/(N+1))|), and imaginary transverse displacement b_j=t_j cos(Nt_j/2)=(-1)^j t_j cos(πj/(N+1)). For a simple real baseline zero, changing to the real coordinate u=Re G and integrating sqrt(u²+ε²b²)−|u| gives b² ε² log(1/|ε|)/|D'| plus O(ε²). Sum all N zeros; the complement is twice differentiable. The remaining finite sum is a Riemann sum yielding the exact limit. Independently checked formula and centered numerical second differences for N=2,4,6 and the N=1000 convergence. No assertion for odd N or uniform joint N,ε.

The local square-root modulus singularity is classical analysis, but exact assembly of its N Dirichlet-zero weights and the universal large-N coefficient is not identified as a published formula.

value.rationale: The failure of twice differentiability in a natural frequency direction and exact positive logarithmic curvature quantify local sensitivity of the classical Dirichlet sum under nonharmonic frequency perturbations; the sharp complete-zero coefficient and its stable limit are useful for frequency-stability questions.

final_claim: For each fixed even N≥2, displacing the highest frequency N by ε in ∑_{k=0}^{N−1}e^{ikt}+e^{i(N+ε)t} changes its [-π,π] L¹ norm by A_N ε + C_N ε² log(1/|ε|)+O_N(ε²), with explicit positive Dirichlet-zero coefficient C_N=16π²/(N+1)^3∑_{j=1}^{N/2}j² sin(πj/(N+1))cos²(πj/(N+1)) and limit 32(3π−7)/(27π).
